questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
CKAD requires practical mastery of node-scoped components, DaemonSets, hostPath volumes, and real-world log shipping patterns.

## Key Concepts
- DaemonSet on each node with hostPath volumes
- Log tailing with tail -F and sidecar shipping
- ConfigMap-driven batching (BATCH_SIZE)
- NodeSelector to target workers
- Readiness/Liveness probes and lifecycle (preStop)
- Resource requests/limits and rollback strategy

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: log-collector
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: log-collector
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: log-collector
    spec:
      nodeSelector:
        kubernetes.io/os: linux
      containers:
      - name: collector
        image: busybox:stable
        command: ["sh","-c","tail -F /var/log/app.log | /usr/local/bin/shipper --endpoint http://log-portal:5000/api/v1/logs --batch-size $(BUS_BATCH)" ]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /var/log
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "256Mi"
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 15
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 30
          periodSeconds: 30
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["sh","-c","sleep 10"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /var/log
      volumes:
      - name: logs
        hostPath:
          path: /var/log
          type: Directory
``` 

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test under burst log loads and verify end-to-end delivery? 
- How would you rollback a DaemonSet rollout if a regression is found?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests knowledge of admission webhooks, namespace-scoped control, and per-namespace policy management. It also touches TLS, RBAC, and logging considerations in Kubernetes.

## Key Concepts
- ValidatingWebhookConfiguration with NamespaceSelector
- Per-namespace ConfigMap policy
- Pod securityContext checks (runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem)
- TLS setup, CA trust, and logging to a PVC

## Code Example
```yaml
# webhook Deployment skeleton
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ns-security-webhook
  namespace: webhooks
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: ns-security-webhook
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ns-security-webhook
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: ns-security-sa
      containers:
      - name: webhook
        image: myorg/ns-security-webhook:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8443
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls
          mountPath: /tls
      volumes:
      - name: tls
        secret:
          secretName: ns-security-tls
```

```yaml
# ValidatingWebhookConfiguration with NamespaceSelector
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration
metadata:
  name: ns-security-webhook-config
webhooks:
- name: ns-security.webhook.example.com
  clientConfig:
    service:
      name: ns-security-webhook
      namespace: webhooks
      path: "/validate"
    caBundle: <base64-CA-cert>
  rules:
  - apiGroups: [""]
    apiVersions: ["v1"]
    operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
    resources: ["pods"]
  namespaceSelector:
    matchLabels:
      webhook: enabled
  sideEffects: None
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to safely patch CronJobs, leverage InitContainers for bootstrapping from ConfigMaps, enforce security context non-root, and apply sensible history limits. It also probes operational testing and rollback strategy for scheduled jobs.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob controls: concurrencyPolicy, history limits, startingDeadlineSeconds
- InitContainers and ConfigMaps for bootstrapping
- PodSecurityContext: runAsNonRoot
- Probes on Jobs' pods and resource requests/limits
- Testing and rollback of scheduled jobs

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal CronJob patch outline (conceptual)
apiVersion: batch/v1beta1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: db-backup
  namespace: nightly
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  startingDeadlineSeconds: 3600
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: backup-sa
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
          initContainers:
            - name: init-backup
              image: busybox
              command: ["sh", "-c", "cp /config/backup.sh /backup/backup.sh"]
              volumeMounts:
                - name: backup-config
                  mountPath: /config
                - name: backups
                  mountPath: /backup
          containers:
            - name: backup
              image: backup-tool:latest
              resources:
                requests:
                  memory: "128Mi"
                  cpu: "100m"
                limits:
                  memory: "256Mi"
                  cpu: "500m"
              readinessProbe:
                httpGet:
                  path: /livez
                  port: 8080
              livenessProbe:
                httpGet:
                  path: /readyz
                  port: 8080
              volumeMounts:
                - name: backups
                  mountPath: /backups
          volumes:
            - name: backups
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: backups-pvc
            - name: backup-config
              configMap:
                name: backup-config
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you monitor backup duration and alert on failures?
- How would you handle a failed run without losing data?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates understanding of in-cluster automation patterns within CKAD scope: PVC-based manifest storage, ConfigMap-driven templating, InitContainers for tool preparation, Secret management for credentials, TLS sidecars for certificate rotation, and NetworkPolicy for egress control. It tests the ability to design operational solutions that balance functionality with security and maintainability.

## Key Concepts

- **In-cluster manifest application**: Using kubectl directly within pods for declarative resource management
- **Template rendering**: Leveraging ConfigMaps for parameterized manifest generation
- **InitContainers**: Preparing runtime dependencies (kubectl, yq) before main container starts
- **Secret management**: Securely storing API credentials for external service integration
- **TLS certificate rotation**: Sidecar pattern for automatic certificate updates without pod disruption
- **NetworkPolicy**: Namespace-level egress restrictions to limit blast radius
- **RBAC**: ServiceAccount with scoped permissions for least-privilege access
- **Probes**: Readiness and liveness checks for operator reliability

## Evaluation Criteria

Strong candidates will address:
1. Proper RBAC scoping to namespace-level permissions
2. Idempotent manifest application using `kubectl apply`
3. Security considerations around elevated pod privileges
4. Trade-offs between simplicity and operational overhead
5. Handling of template rendering and variable substitution

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests CKAD fundamentals in a practical way: probes, resources, and ConfigMap usage. It checks that the candidate can translate requirements into Kubernetes primitives and reason about reliability.

## Key Concepts
- Liveness vs readiness probes
- Resource requests and limits
- ConfigMaps as configuration and env binding
- Volume mounts and envFrom/KeyRefs

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web-app
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web-app
        image: registry.example.com/web-app:v1.2
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8080
          timeoutSeconds: 3
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: 250m
            memory: 256Mi
          limits:
            cpu: 500m
            memory: 512Mi
        env:
        - name: APP_MODE
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: web-app-config
              key: APP_MODE
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config-volume
          mountPath: /etc/config
      volumes:
      - name: config-volume
        configMap:
```

Tests practical CKAD debugging: handling slow-start upgrades with probes, init containers for bootstrapping state, and PD&B safeguards to prevent downtime during maintenance.

## Key Concepts

- startupProbe and readinessProbe tuning
- initContainer for pre-warming caches
- PodDisruptionBudget for upgrade safety
- RollingUpdate strategy and rollback procedures

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal patch sketch (Deployment snippet)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: invoice-processor
  namespace: payments
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: init-cache
        image: invoice-processor:2.1
        command: ["sh", "-c", "cp /config/* /var/cache/ || true"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config
          mountPath: /config
        - name: cache
          mountPath: /var/cache
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: invoice-processor:2.1
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 30
          periodSeconds: 10
      volumes:
      - name: config
        secret:
          secretName: app-secret
      - name: cache
        emptyDir: {}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you adapt this for a cluster with limited CPU headroom?
- What metrics would you monitor to confirm startup health and cache warmth?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD skills: scoped RBAC, InitContainers, per-namespace automation, and secure egress.

## Key Concepts
- Namespace-scoped CronJob and RBAC
- InitContainer installation of tooling (Trivy)
- Enumerating images from Deployments in a namespace
- Secret-based Bearer token auth and external POST
- Logs via PVC and network policy constraints

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal CronJob skeleton (yaml)
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: image-scan
  namespace: default
spec:
  schedule: "*/20 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
            - name: install-trivy
              image: alpine:3.18
              command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl git && true"]
          containers:
            - name: scanner
              image: alpine:3.18
              command: ["sh", "-c", "echo scanning..."]
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle image pull secrets rotation and audit logging for scans?
- What trade-offs exist between scan frequency, image cache, and registry rate limits?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to compose CKAD primitives: ConfigMaps for runtime knobs, Secrets for credentials, InitContainers for bootstrapping assets, PVCs for content, and NetworkPolicy for egress control, all in a per-namespace scope.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainers, ConfigMaps, Secrets, PVCs
- Liveness/Readiness probes
- NetworkPolicy, egress controls
- Static site hosting with nginx

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal Deployment skeleton (conceptual)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: static-site
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:alpine
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html
          name: html
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 80
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 80
      initContainers:
      - name: fetch-assets
        image: appropriate/cull
        # placeholder for fetch logic using site-config
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /html
          name: html
      volumes:
      - name: html
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: site-pvc
      # ... Secrets/ConfigMaps mounted as envs or files
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle asset updates without redeploying pods?
- What are the security implications of mounting secrets vs. env vars in this setup?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical batch-job composition: init tooling, config-driven scripts, and safe cleanup. 

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes Job TTL, backoff, and completion semantics
- InitContainers alongside main containers
- ConfigMap and Secret mounts; env from Secret
- Resource requests/limits; idempotence

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: db-migrate
  namespace: migrate
spec:
  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 600
  backoffLimit: 3
  completions: 1
  parallelism: 1
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: install-tools
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh","-c","apk add --no-cache postgresql-client"]
      containers:
        - name: migrate
          image: postgres:15
          envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: db-creds
          env:
            - name: PGHOST
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: db-creds
                  key: host
          command: ["psql","-h","$(PGHOST)","-U","$(POSTGRES_USER)","-d","migration_db","-f","/migrate/scripts/migrate.sql"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: migrate-scripts
              mountPath: /migrate/scripts
      volumes:
        - name: migrate-scripts
          configMap:
            name: migrate-scripts
      restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate idempotence for repeated runs?
- How would you rollback if migration fails after partial progress?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical CKAD skills: wiring ConfigMaps and Secrets, configuring InitContainers, implementing TLS sidecars, setting up readiness/liveness probes, and crafting a NetworkPolicy with conditional egress.

## Key Concepts
- ConfigMap-driven feature flags
- Secrets for credential management
- InitContainers for tooling installation
- TLS sidecars for secure communication
- Readiness and liveness probe configuration
- Namespace NetworkPolicy for egress control

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: feature-config
data:
  ENABLE_API: "true"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: api-creds
type: Opaque
data:
  token: <base64-encoded-token>
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: app-namespace
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: egress-policy
  namespace: app-namespace
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    - to:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: internal-api
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 8080
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: my-app
  namespace: app-namespace
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: my-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: my-app
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: installer
          image: curlimages/curl:latest
          command: ['sh', '-c', 'echo Initialized']
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: my-app:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          env:
            - name: ENABLE_API
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: feature-config
                  key: ENABLE_API
            - name: API_TOKEN
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: api-creds
                  key: token
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /status
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /status
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 20
        - name: tls-sidecar
          image: nginx:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 443
```

## Trade-offs
- **NetworkPolicy complexity**: The policy above allows egress only to the internal-api pod. A more permissive approach might allow DNS resolution but restrict target services.
- **InitContainer overhead**: Installing curl in every pod increases startup time and image size. Consider baking tools into the base image if startup latency is critical.
- **Sidecar maintenance**: A TLS sidecar adds complexity and resource overhead. For simple use cases, TLS could be handled within the application container directly.
- **Secret security**: Storing credentials in a Secret is fine for basic scenarios, but consider external secrets operators or vault integration for production environments requiring rotation.
- **Probe configuration**: Aggressive probe settings can cause unnecessary restarts; conservative settings may delay failure detection. Tune based on application startup time.
